saints.name: St. Francis de Sales
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The gentle bishop of Geneva who taught that holiness is for everyone and won souls back by patience and love…
biography: Born on 21 August 1567 at the castle of Sales in Savoy, Francis was bred to the law and took his doctorate at Padua, but refused a senator's place and was ordained priest in 1593. Sent into the Chablais, where Calvinism ruled, he won the country back in four years, as much by leaflets slipped under doors and by patience as by argument.

Consecrated bishop of Geneva in 1602, he resided at Annecy, Geneva itself being closed to him. His Introduction to the Devout Life, printed in 1609, taught that holiness belongs to every state of life, and with Jane Frances de Chantal he founded the Visitation Order in 1610 for women unequal to the austerities of the older orders. The Treatise on the Love of God followed in 1616.

He died at Lyons on 28 December 1622, worn out at fifty-five, and was canonized by Alexander VII in 1665; Pius IX named him Doctor of the Church in 1877. Because he evangelized by the printed page, Pius XI declared him patron of writers and journalists in 1923, and because he taught the catechism by signs to a deaf-mute, he is patron likewise of the deaf.
saints.knownFor: Teaching that holiness is possible for everyone.

canonization.canonized: 1665 by Pope Alexander VII; Doctor of the Church (1877)
